t:
(a) Assessment.—The Commandant of the Coast Guard, in consultation with the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the head of any other agency 
the Commandant determines appropriate, shall conduct an assessment of the effectiveness of oil spill response activities specific to the Great Lakes. Such assessment shall include—
        (1) an evaluation of new research into oil spill impacts in fresh water under a wide range of conditions; and 
        (2) an evaluation of oil spill prevention and clean up contingency plans, in order to improve understanding of oil spill impacts in the Great Lakes and foster innovative improvements to safety technologies and environmental protection systems.  
    (b) Report to Congress.—Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commandant of the Coast Guard shall submit to the Congress a report on the results of the assessment required by subsection (a).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "consultation" and the formal report signal participation. But the consultation is only between the Coast Guard Commandant, the NOAA Administrator and other agency heads, all federal officials, and the report goes to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is brought into any federal decision, and the section concerns an assessment rather than a rulemaking or other decision.
fable.s: in consultation with the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

opus.w: The only consultation named is between the Coast Guard and NOAA or other agencies, which is coordination inside the federal government. The report goes to Congress, which is also inside the government. The word "consultation" makes this look like participation, but no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is brought in. The assessment is also a study, not a federal policy decision.
opus.s:
The Commandant of the Coast Guard, in consultation with the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the head of any other agency 
the Commandant determines appropriate, shall conduct an assessment

qwen_chat.w: The section requires consultation between federal officials (Commandant of the Coast Guard, Administrator of NOAA, and other agency heads). According to the definition, consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not constitute participation. The resulting report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. No outside parties are involved in the assessment or decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Commandant of the Coast Guard, in consultation with the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the head of any other agency the Commandant determines appropriate, shall conduct an assessment...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation" with the Administrator of NOAA and other agency heads constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not count as participation. All actors mentioned (Commandant of the Coast Guard, Administrator of NOAA, heads of other agencies) are inside the federal government. The report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, private entities) in the decision-making process described.
